title: Adult sepsis and septic shock (India)

symptoms: Fever or feeling abnormally cold; rigors and profound malaise.
Breathlessness, confusion or reduced urine; ask about respiratory, urinary, abdominal, skin and device symptoms.
physicalSigns: Hypotension, tachypnoea, altered mentation, mottling or delayed capillary refill; fever may be absent.
Examine the chest, abdomen, skin, joints and indwelling devices for a source.
redFlags: Persistent hypotension, increasing oxygen requirement, reduced consciousness or progressive organ dysfunction: request critical care immediately.
Septic shock criteria: vasopressors needed to maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP) at least 65 mmHg plus lactate above 2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation (Sepsis-3, Box 3).
precipitants: Pneumonia; urinary or intra-abdominal infection; infected skin, tissue or vascular devices.
Recent hospitalisation, prior resistant isolates and recent broad-spectrum treatment change empirical choices (NCDC–ICMR, section 3.4; SSC 2026, section Multidrug resistance).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Cardiac dysfunction or congestion on bedside ultrasound; fluids may worsen pulmonary oedema. Assess alongside infection.
Bleeding or fluid loss with a compatible examination; investigate and treat the cause rather than assuming infection.
Acute unexplained hypoxaemia or right-heart strain; use the pulmonary embolism pathway if suspected.

differentials.condition: Dengue or malaria with organ dysfunction
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Exposure and targeted testing redirect management; a positive result does not exclude bacterial co-infection.
Drug reaction, pancreatitis or another non-infectious diagnosis may explain the presentation; revisit the infection diagnosis at every review.

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults in India; six-tier source-based revision. Clinical review pending.
findings: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR): joint Version 2.0, November 2025 verified directly on the title page. World Health Organization (WHO) guidance is supplementary.

India regional topic. Indian national antimicrobial guidance takes precedence over older ICMR text. WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) warnings identify stewardship category, not an automatic indication. Check hospital formulary, product strength and local antibiogram. No Saudi registration claim is made for this India adaptation.
unverifiedSections: Hospital antibiogram, stocked Indian product licences, local infusion preparation and operational referral arrangements require local clinical/pharmacy confirmation.
The proposed 48-hour antibiotic authorisation cap is an explicitly labelled Marifa governance proposal requiring clinician/pharmacy sign-off, not an endorsed national total-course limit.
Risk-triggered glycopeptide selection differs from the default NCDC undifferentiated-shock combination and is shown in guidelineComparison.
SFDA registration is outside this India scope. NLEM listing is not proof of a specific stocked brand licence.

ruleIn.normalValue: Alert at baseline; SOFA neurologic reference is Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 15; assess circulation against the patient baseline.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: New confusion, hypotension or impaired peripheral perfusion.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record trends during resuscitation; do not use a screening score alone to exclude sepsis.

ruleIn.normalValue: Fasting venous reference 0.5–2.2 mmol/L; assay range is not a sepsis decision threshold.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Lactate >2 mmol/L triggers repeat measurement in the Indian bundle; ≥4 mmol/L is an Indian fluid-bundle trigger.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Repeat if initially >2 mmol/L and interpret alongside perfusion; worsening acidosis or lactate requires senior reassessment.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Creatinine rises or urine output falls relative to baseline.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Assess renal injury and electrolyte disturbance; review every renally cleared antibiotic and fluid balance.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Bilirubin elevation or other hepatic injury.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Assess organ dysfunction and hepatic drug cautions; examine for biliary obstruction.

medicationPlan.note: India regional topic. Indian national antimicrobial guidance takes precedence over older ICMR text. WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) warnings identify stewardship category, not an automatic indication. Check hospital formulary, product strength and local antibiogram. No Saudi registration claim is made for this India adaptation. Branches are patient selections, not a list to administer together. Additional risk-triggered branches apply only when their entry condition is met. Empirical prescribing block: mandatory review and active renewal at 48 hours. No source-independent total-course maximum exists; renewal requires an organism/site-specific duration and calendar stop date. Proposed Marifa control, not a national treatment-duration rule.

branches.label: Community sepsis without shock
branches.entryCriteria: Community-onset suspected bacterial sepsis without shock and without a localised syndrome requiring a different regimen.

branches.label: Undifferentiated septic shock
branches.entryCriteria: Community-onset shock without a source, or hospital-onset sepsis with high resistant Gram-negative risk; validate against local antibiogram.

branches.label: Add-on resistant Gram-positive cover
branches.entryCriteria: Enter only with a resistant Gram-positive risk requiring coverage, such as a suspected vascular-device infection or previous relevant isolate; accompany the selected backbone.

branches.label: Suspected rickettsial infection
branches.entryCriteria: Compatible endemic exposure and clinical suspicion; an add-on to the selected sepsis backbone, not an automatic component for all fever.

branches.label: Hypoperfusion
branches.entryCriteria: Sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock requiring fluid resuscitation.

branches.label: Persistent hypotension
branches.entryCriteria: Hypotension despite an initial fluid challenge, or unstable shock while fluids are being given.

adjustments: Creatinine clearance 20–40 mL/min: maximum 4.5 g every 8 hours; <20: maximum 4.5 g every 12 hours. Hepatic impairment: no dose change (SmPC section 4.2).
India NLEM 2022 section 6.2.1.13 lists 4 g/0.5 g injection. Check hospital formulary.

Monitor renal function, electrolytes, blood count, allergy and diarrhoea; combined vancomycin increases renal-toxicity concern.
contraindications: Do not rely on it for confirmed ceftriaxone-resistant extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) E. coli or Klebsiella bacteraemia (SmPC section 4.1).

Monitor renal function, blood count, liver tests and seizures.

pathophysiology.summary: Sepsis is infection-associated organ dysfunction; septic shock adds persistent circulatory and metabolic failure (Sepsis-3, Box 3). Supportive care uses the Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) 2026 update.
keyMechanisms: An uncontrolled host response to infection injures organs beyond the initial site (Sepsis-3, Box 3).
Vasodilation and altered microcirculation impair tissue perfusion; resuscitation must balance perfusion against fluid overload (SSC 2026, section Resuscitation).
A rise in Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score of at least 2 supports infection-related organ dysfunction; it is not a prerequisite for treatment (Sepsis-3, Box 3).
Raised lactate needs clinical interpretation: it supports risk assessment but does not independently prove infection (SSC 2026, section Serial lactate).

clinicalScenario: Fictitious teaching case: an adult with fever and new confusion arrives hypotensive after recent antibiotic exposure. Assess infection likelihood, perfusion and an anatomical source while obtaining cultures; do not wait for a score or microbiology result to treat shock.

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise, stabilise and classify infection likelihood
actions: Assess airway, breathing and circulation; provide monitored care and call the senior clinician. Record the recognition time.

Request intensive care unit (ICU) support for shock, impaired airway protection or worsening respiratory/organ failure. Do not wait for the SOFA calculation (SSC 2026, sections Fluid resuscitation and ICU admission).
Give appropriate antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour; obtain cultures without delaying therapy (SSC 2026, section Antibiotic initiation).
Investigate rapidly; if infection concern persists, administer antimicrobials within 3 hours of first suspicion (SSC 2026, section Antibiotic initiation).

branches.condition: Low likelihood of infection without shock
actions: Withhold antibiotics while continuing reassessment and investigating alternatives (SSC 2026, section Antibiotic initiation).

clinicalManagement.title: Restore perfusion with reassessment
actions: For sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or shock, SSC 2026 suggests at least 30 mL/kg intravenous crystalloid in the first 3 hours, individualised to clinical context. Prefer balanced crystalloid; reassess after each bolus and stop further boluses if congestion or lack of responsiveness develops (SSC 2026, sections Fluid resuscitation and Fluid type).
Use a passive-leg-raise or measured response to a fluid challenge where available, alongside capillary refill, lactate, mental state and urine output (SSC 2026, section Resuscitation).

Start noradrenaline for persistent hypotension; unstable shock may need vasopressors alongside fluids. Initial MAP target 65 mmHg; for adults ≥65 years, SSC 2026 suggests 60–65 mmHg, individualised by the critical-care clinician (SSC 2026, sections Fluid resuscitation and Mean arterial pressure).

Do not delay a necessary vasopressor solely to obtain central access. Use a local peripheral-vasopressor protocol with site surveillance until central access is established; the product-specific preparation and peripheral concentration require pharmacy confirmation (SSC 2026, section Vasopressor administration).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose one empirical branch and obtain source control
clinicalManagement.timeframe: With initial antibiotics; source control ideally within 6 hours
actions: Use the medication branch matching community sepsis without shock, undifferentiated septic shock, or hospital-acquired infection. Do not stack these antibiotic backbones. A localised infection uses its site-specific pathway (NCDC–ICMR, section 3.4).
Select additional resistant Gram-positive cover from documented risk and the local antibiogram; avoid routine broadening in a low-risk patient (SSC 2026, section Multidrug resistance).

Suspected obstruction, abscess, perforation, necrotising tissue or infected device requires an urgent procedural plan; aim for source control within 6 hours when indicated (SSC 2026, section Source control).

clinicalManagement.title: Review cultures, narrow treatment and set the stop date
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Daily; mandatory empirical review at 48 hours
actions: Check organism, susceptibility, source control, response and drug toxicity. Stop unnecessary components; negative cultures with improvement support de-escalation (NCDC–ICMR, section 3.4, p. 29; SSC 2026, section Antimicrobial therapy).

Proposed Marifa prescribing safeguard: the empirical antibiotic authorisation expires at the 48-hour review and must be actively renewed with a diagnosis, total-course duration and calendar stop date. This is a review/renewal cap, not an instruction to discontinue essential therapy in unstable sepsis and not an Indian national total-course maximum.
For a confirmed focus, apply its organism- and site-specific duration; count all effective treatment already given. Do not invent a blanket sepsis course length (NCDC–ICMR, section 3.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate refractory illness and plan recovery
actions: Escalate worsening lactate, mentation, oxygenation or vasopressor requirement immediately; reassess shock type, source control, drug exposure and resistant pathogens (SSC 2026, sections Resuscitation and Vasopressors).
For patients needing ICU admission, SSC 2026 suggests transfer within 6 hours. Use monitored transfer with an accepting team and a documented infusion plan.

Before discharge reconcile medicines, explain the infection and residual problems, and give a written treatment stop date and follow-up ownership (SSC 2026, sections Transitions of care and Hospital discharge).

patientEducation: Explain the infection, organ effects and the reason for urgent treatment.
Give written return advice for recurrent fever, breathlessness, confusion or reduced urine.
Provide the antibiotic indication and calendar stop date; do not retain leftovers.
lifestyleAndDiet: Resume oral/enteral nutrition when safe; assess swallowing, weakness and rehabilitation needs.
Review vaccination, chronic disease care and modifiable infection risks after stabilisation.
mdtReferrals: Critical care for shock, respiratory failure or deteriorating consciousness.
Surgery, urology or interventional radiology for a source needing drainage or removal.
Microbiology/infectious diseases and pharmacy for resistant organisms, severe allergy, renal replacement therapy or unclear duration.
dischargeCriteria: Haemodynamic and respiratory stability without escalating support.
Source controlled or a documented accepted follow-up plan exists.
Culture review completed or a named clinician owns pending results.
Medication reconciliation, stop dates, mobility/support and follow-up are documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Arrange an individual follow-up and rehabilitation plan before discharge; hand over residual organ dysfunction, pending cultures and responsibility for antibiotic completion (SSC 2026, sections Hospital discharge and Transitions of care).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Suspected or confirmed infection with an acute SOFA increase ≥2 (Sepsis-3, Box 3).
Sepsis plus vasopressor requirement to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg and lactate >2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation (Sepsis-3, Box 3).

guidelineComparison.title: Indian national baseline and current international supportive-care guidance

values: Section 3.4 pp. 30–31: 30 mL/kg rapidly for hypotension or lactate ≥4 mmol/L.
Fluid resuscitation: at least 30 mL/kg in the first 3 hours for hypoperfusion/shock, individualised with repeated reassessment.
Section 3.4 p. 29: undifferentiated community shock table includes a glycopeptide with the carbapenem.
Multidrug resistance: cover a resistant pathogen when risk is high; avoid routine coverage when risk is low. Risk-based branch selection needs local stewardship sign-off.
Section 3.4: source, organism and clinical course determine duration; de-escalation review at 48 hours.
No universal total-course maximum. Proposed Marifa 48-hour empirical authorisation expiry is a review safeguard, not a national treatment stop.
Mean arterial pressure: general initial target 65 mmHg; adults ≥65 years may start at 60–65 mmHg with clinical individualisation.

guidelineComparison.note: Differences are not blended into a new numerical range; local clinicians must approve the operational pathway.

teaching.scope: Adult India sepsis recognition, initial resuscitation and source-directed stewardship.
learningObjectives: Separate possible infection from probable sepsis and shock.
Select one antibiotic backbone and only indicated add-ons.
Reassess fluids and document source control and an antibiotic stop date.
keyPoints: Do not wait for a score in unstable sepsis.
Local resistance and source drive therapy.
A 48-hour review is not a universal completed course.
pitfalls: Treating every fever with a carbapenem.
Continuing all empirical medicines after cultures clarify the diagnosis.
